    Extending arrows (Definition 4.2) #

    For a string w over special biserial monomial data, an arrow c is an outgoing extending arrow at a position p if it starts at the vertex of p and is compatible with the edges at p: it differs from the label of every outgoing edge, and it is an allowed successor of the label of every incoming edge. Dually for incoming extending arrows. At an endpoint this is the table of Section 4.1.

    isEnd_and_outExt shows: a position over src b without an outgoing b-edge and without incoming edges labelled by a forbidden predecessor of b is an endpoint at which b is an outgoing extending arrow. An internal position would need two incident edges, which contradicts the special biserial bounds or the string condition. isEnd_and_inExt is the mirror statement.
